I farm the way I always have: I start from what worked last year, then I push a little if I think the crop can pay me back. I have 15 mu total, and with wheat-maize rotation I will keep 10 mu in wheat first, then plant maize on that same 10 mu after wheat harvest. The other 5 mu I will keep in cotton. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard, because if yield falls, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on two more bags. Around here, if wheat has water and enough base fertilizer, it can give a steady crop. Maize after wheat has to catch time fast, so I will use hybrid seed and feed it stronger. Cotton is slower and needs more watching for insects, so I will not plant too much of it, only what my family can manage well. With well water in hand, I will give wheat about 3 irrigations, maize 2, and cotton 3, depending on rain. I will plough for wheat and cotton, and after wheat I will mostly use rotary tillage to turn maize around quickly. I watch what fields around me do, but I still hold a little extra fertilizer in mind because a bad harvest is worse than wasting some input.
